title: Annotatio IV §.XV close: not consubstantiation patron — Rupert charges bare sign; more in Annot. 3 — stop
pass_a_gloss: Although indeed from these and similar words Berengar has customarily been wrongly conjectured by some as Favorer and Patron of Consubstantiation, yet that he is by no means to be numbered among these even Rupert Abbot of Deutz himself, first and chief Author of Crasser Consubstantiation, will freely confess, when he makes Berengar not only the standard-bearer of those erring but also locates his error in this — that he wished the Sacrament of the Lord’s body and blood to be held a bare sign of the sacred thing. For so Rupert the Consubstantiator attacks the Confessors of Truth: But what they say, what they bring forward as argument, he says, they do not have, except that some of them, while they wish the Sacrament of the Lord’s body and blood to be only a sign of the sacred thing, according to the former error of Berengar of Tours … even think Blessed Augustine feels so (On the Eucharistic Sacrament Book 3 ch. 11 and 15). The rest to be said concerning Berengar seek above in Annot. 3.
pass_b_english: Some wrongly make Berengar a consubstantiation patron — even Rupert of Deutz (crasser consubstantiation’s chief author) refuses that and instead charges him with wanting a bare sign of the sacred thing.
Rupert attacks truth-confessors as having no argument but that bare-sign claim (ascribed also to Augustine). Rest on Berengar: see above, Annot. 3. Stop before §.XVI / next extract.
source_text: Etsi verò ex his similibusque verbis, perperam à nonnullis, Berengarius Consubstantiationis Fautor & Patronus conjecturari consuevit, tamen annumerandum hisce minimè esse vel ipse Rupertus Abbas Tuitiensis, Consubstantiationis Crassioris Auctor, primus & præcipuus, fateri ultrò nullus verebitur, quando Berengarium non tantum errantium Antesignanum facit, sed & errorem ejus in eo collocat, quod Sacramentum corporis & sanguinis Domini, nudum rei sacræ signum voluerit haberi. Ita enim Rupertus Consubstantiator, Veritatis Confessores oppugnat: Illi autem quid dicant, quid pro argumento afferant, inquit, non habent, nisi quod aliqui ex iis, dum volunt Sacramentum corporis & sanguinis Domini, solummodò signum esse sacræ rei, juxta errorem quondam Berengarii Turonensis … etiam B. Augustinum sentire ita putant (De Sacramento Eucharistico lib. 3. cap. 11. & 15.). Cetera de Berengario dicenda require suprà Annot. 3.

lemmas.gloss: a bare sign of the sacred thing

notes: Not consubstantiation; Rupert bare-sign charge; Annot.3.
